newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs lean on 5.60% support, seen testing it.
newsitem.headline: OLOs lean on 5.60% support, seen testing it.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds and futures leaned on a double, technical threshold on Wednesday.
Dealers expected the market to test and break 5.60 percent yields for 10-year cash OLOs BE286= and 122.50 for the September futures contract BGBc1 soon.
OLO futures, up 36 bps at 122.48 at 1235 GMT, stopped short of 122.50, a resistance level set on June 17, while cash OLOs dipped to 5.59 from 5.63 percent late on Tuesday.
"I can see a serious test of 5.60," one dealer said. There the market was still liquid enough to attract new bond investments.
The next targets are the February 18 high of 123.83, which corresponded to a cash 10-year yield of about 5.50 percent.
Bund futures' break above 103 was seen as a positive signal.

One dealer warned the market could see a selloff after a seven-day winning streak. Players had for now chosen to ignore doubts about Paris' commitment to EMU budget rigour, but when the French 1998 budget was drafted in the autumn, markets could become very nervous.
The 10-year OLO yield spread over Bunds was one bp higher at eight bps. French OATs yielded eight bps less than Bunds MEUR.

Money market yields were virtually unchanged. Three-month Belgian deposit yields, at 3.28 percent TTFBXL, were 22 bps over their German equivalents despite economists' forecasts that the short-term spread would narrow soon.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
